data.name: Pawankumar
data.gender_notes: Pawankumar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Pawan refers to the wind god, and Kumar means young or prince. Pawankumar can be translated as the 'Lord of the Forest' or 'Young Prince of the Wind'. The name Pawankumar carries the meaning “Lord of the Forest” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit. Parents who choose Pawankumar usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the forest and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Pawankumar is a name that signifies power, strength, and leadership. It is believed that individuals with this name possess the ability to command respect and influence those around them.
data.etymology: Pawankumar belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Forest.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Pawankumar total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: Pawankumar is a Hindi name that has strong associations with Hindu mythology and the natural world. It reflects a deep respect for the power and majesty of nature, particularly the wind, as Pawan is the Hindu god of wind and air. The name Pawankumar also carries the imprint of the rich cultural heritage of India, where the divine and the natural are inextricably intertwined.
data.spiritual_significance: Pawankumar is a name that connects its bearer to the divine forces of nature. It is a constant reminder to remain grounded and to find peace in the natural world. The name Pawankumar is also a symbol of the spiritual growth that comes from facing challenges and obstacles. Just as the wind can be forceful and unpredictable, so too can life present us with difficult situations. But by embracing adversity with the grace, wisdom, and courage of a prince, one can grow into a truly awesome individual, revered and cherished by all.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Pawan signifies the wind god, symbolizing change and movement in life. Kumar represents young Lord Shiva, symbolizing strength, wisdom, and devotion. Together, Pawankumar embodies the dynamic force of change guided by the wisdom and devotion of the young Lord Shiva.

historical_references.reference: Pawankumar Chauhan was a Rajput warrior who fought against the Muslim invader Alauddin Khilji in the 13th century. He was the commander of Raja Ratan Singh of Chitorgarh and defended the fort against Khilji's forces. However, he was eventually captured and executed.
historical_references.context: Medieval India, Rajput resistance against Muslim invaders

historical_references.reference: Pawankumar (also known as Panakkal Narayana Bhagavatar) was a 16th century Hindu reformer and philosopher who challenged the prevailing Orthodoxy of Hinduism. He advocated for the worship of Vishnu in the form of Krishna and criticized the caste system and idolatry.
